claims.statement: Meta documents an App Secret that Meta assigns to each Meta app, found in the App Dashboard basic settings, and that must be stored securely and kept out of client-side code.

sources.supports: find the app secret assigned to your app by Meta
It is extremely important that an App Secret be stored securely and not be included in any code that could be accessed by anyone other than a developer of the app.

claims.statement: Meta states the App Secret is reset in the Basic Settings of the App Dashboard, that it cannot be rotated programmatically, and that Meta may itself reset it when it discovers a leak that puts user data at risk.

sources.supports: It is not possible to programmatically rotate the app secret.
If you do not reply in a timely manner, Meta will reset the app secret.
sources.locator: Basic Settings, Resetting App Secret, Note

claims.statement: Meta documents two carriers of the App Secret in server-side calls: the client_secret query parameter of the oauth/access_token call (with client_id and grant_type client_credentials) that returns an app access token, and, instead of a generated token, the string {app-id}|{app-secret} (app ID, a pipe, the app secret) passed as the access_token parameter. The app ID is the leading part of the second form; the page does not say the app ID is non-secret.

sources.supports: To generate an app access token, you need: Your App ID, Your App Secret
sources.locator: App Access Tokens, Generating an app access token

sources.supports: You can just pass your app ID and app secret as the `access_token` parameter when you make a call
sources.locator: App Access Tokens, Generating an app access token

claims.statement: Meta documents appsecret_proof as a sha256 hash of an access token using the app secret as the key (the page's example computes it with hash_hmac and sha256), added as a request parameter. It is an output computed from the secret and a token; the page does not state its encoding or length and does not say whether it is safe to disclose.

sources.supports: The app secret proof is a sha256 hash of your access token, using your app secret as the key.
sources.locator: Verify Graph API Calls with appsecret_proof
Verify Graph API Calls with appsecret_proof, Generate the Proof

claims.statement: Three open-source scanner rule artifacts by different maintainers (Gitleaks, TruffleHog, Nosey Parker) each treat a string of exactly 32 characters appearing next to a facebook-related context word as an application-secret candidate. This records consistency among those artifacts at the pinned commits; it is not a provider statement of the format. The artifacts differ on the alphabet (lowercase hexadecimal in Gitleaks; letters and digits in TruffleHog; lowercase letters and digits with a case-insensitive flag in Nosey Parker), and each gates on a context word, so none treats a bare 32-character value as attributable to Meta.

sources.supports: Rule facebook-secret: a context word 'facebook' followed by an assignment-like separator and a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal capture group.
apiSecretPat: a 'facebook' prefix context followed by a word-bounded capture of exactly 32 alphanumeric characters.

Rule np.facebook.1 (Facebook Secret Key): a facebook or fb context word with app/secret/key words, then a word-bounded capture of exactly 32 lowercase alphanumeric characters (case-insensitive flag set).

claims.statement: No Meta page read states the App Secret's length, alphabet or encoding. The three rule artifacts disagree on the alphabet (hexadecimal only versus any letters and digits), so no alphabet and no length is recorded in the structure; a 32-character length is recorded only as the artifacts' consistent scope in the tool-corroborated claim.

sources.supports: Basic Settings App Secret section states storage and use but no length, alphabet or encoding.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Revision 2 supersedes revision 1 additively. Revision 1 carried structure.length.exact 32, which the schema reserves for a length as defined by the provider; no provider page states one, so this revision removes it from the structure and keeps the 32-character observation as the tool-corroborated claim with the artifacts' scope. The existence claim and the three-artifact claim are restated with the 2026-10-05 re-read.

openQuestions.question: Would a Meta page, SDK source or changelog state the App Secret's length and alphabet? Until one does, a 32-character hexadecimal-looking value cannot be attributed to Meta by shape: the same width and alphabet is common to other digests and identifiers, so the artifacts' agreement rests on a facebook-related context word. Independence of the three artifacts' authors is a reviewer check, not a machine check. An issued sample would be issuance-gated and was not sought.

The Basic Settings page calls the App ID a unique identifier assigned to the app and says it must be included in API calls, but does not call it non-secret (it does say a client token is not secret). The App ID is therefore recorded here only as the leading part of the documented composite, without a public-identifier assertion.
The page names a sha256 hash keyed by the app secret but not its output encoding or length, and does not say whether the proof may be exposed. Not asserted; no sample is recorded.
meta:instagram-app-secret is a separate family; whether the two secrets share a grammar is not established here. Recorded as a boundary, not an answer.
